input.question: Why do taste testers use gold cutlery?
input.ground_truth: Gold is one of the least reactive substances in the world. As a result when your job is tasting extremely subtle things that neutrality is vital. More reactive things like plastic, steel, or silver have a chance of altering the flavor of the food for them. While you and I may not have sophisticated enough tastes to tell the difference they can, and that can affect their job performances.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do taste testers use gold cutlery?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you want to taste a tiny bit of ice cream. If you use a shiny, clean spoon, you know that the spoon didn’t have any old ice cream or yucky stuff on it from before. That way, you taste only the new ice cream, not something old and different.

Gold cutlery is super shiny and easy to clean. It doesn’t have any taste by itself, and it always looks (and is) very clean. That way, taste testers can be sure they are tasting just the food, not the spoon!
